_definition_of_the_fold.text:
THE FOLD (the definition used in every UM-3 file)

Definition. The fold is the seven-dimensional surface of the author's eight-dimensional spacetime on which the cosine of
the angle z = 6 H x0 of the hidden direction vanishes:
    (FD-1)  F = { X = (x0, x1, ..., x7) : cos(6 H x0) = 0 };  in one period 0 < z < pi of the metric: z = pi/2, x0 = pi/(12 H).
X = {x0, ..., x7} are the author's coordinates: x0 the hidden space-like direction, x1, x2, x3 ordinary space, x4 the
time, x5, x6, x7 the three extra times; H is the author's constant (an inverse length). The author's metric depends on x0
only through cot(z)^2 and (sin(z)^2)^(1/6), so it repeats with the period pi/(6 H) of x0, and every period 0 < z < pi
contains exactly one fold, at z = pi/2. A point of the fold is labelled by the seven coordinates x1, ..., x7, and the
metric restricted to the fold (dx0 = 0, z = pi/2) is
    (FD-2)  ds^2 on F = e^(2 a4) (dx1^2 + dx2^2 + dx3^2) - dx4^2 - e^(-2 a4) b4^2 (dx5^2 + dx6^2 + dx7^2),
with three space-like and four time-like directions; a4 and b4 are the author's two functions of the time x4.

Why this surface is called a fold. Measured by the proper distance along the hidden direction,
    (FD-3)  sigma = sgn(pi/2 - z) ln(sin z)/(6 H),   d sigma = |cot z| dx0,   sin z = e^(-6 H |sigma|)
(the fold is sigma = 0; the half-period 0 < z < pi/2 is sigma < 0, the half-period pi/2 < z < pi is sigma > 0; the two ends
of the period, the tips z -> 0 and z -> pi, lie at sigma -> -infinity and sigma -> +infinity), the author's metric is
    (FD-4)  ds^2 = d sigma^2 + e^(-2 H |sigma|) [ e^(2 a4) (dx1^2 + dx2^2 + dx3^2) - e^(-2 a4) b4^2 (dx5^2 + dx6^2 + dx7^2) ] - dx4^2.
It depends on sigma only through |sigma|. Four properties make the surface sigma = 0 a fold, and together they single it
out within the period:
  1. It is a mirror. The reflection sigma -> -sigma (that is z -> pi - z, or x0 -> pi/(6 H) - x0) maps the metric to
     itself, and the fold is the only surface of the period that the reflection leaves in place: the two halves of the
     period are mirror images of each other, joined along the fold, as the two halves of a folded sheet of paper are
     joined along the crease.
  2. The warp is largest on it. The warp factor (sin(z)^2)^(1/6) = e^(-2 H |sigma|), which multiplies ordinary space and
     the extra times, equals 1 on the fold and decreases on both sides.
  3. The metric has a kink on it. The metric is continuous across the fold, but its first derivative along sigma jumps.
     The extrinsic curvature of the surfaces sigma = const changes sign across the fold,
        (FD-5)  K^a_b = (1/2) g^ac d_sigma g_cb:  K^1_1 = K^2_2 = K^3_3 = K^5_5 = K^6_6 = K^7_7 = -H sgn(sigma),  K^4_4 = 0;
     (g_ab the metric components along the fold, g^ab their inverse, d_sigma the derivative with respect to sigma, sgn the
     sign function); it jumps by -2 H along ordinary space and along the extra times. The Einstein-Lovelock equations are
     linear in the second sigma-derivatives of the metric, so the jump puts a Dirac delta function delta_D(sigma) into
     them: the metric solves them only if the fold carries a thin source S^a_b, an energy-momentum tensor concentrated on
     sigma = 0 (the junction conditions). At the author's vacuum (a4' = H, b4 constant) its frame components along (ordinary space, the
     time, the extra times) are kappa S = (-10 H, -6 H, -10 H), at the static late-time state (a4 and b4 constant)
     kappa S = (-61 H/8, -31 H/4, -61 H/8), with kappa = 8 pi G_8 the gravitational coupling of eight dimensions. The fold
     is therefore not only a place but a physical object: a thin layer that carries energy and momentum (a brane).
  4. The author's coordinate x0 degenerates on it. The metric component g_x0x0 = cot(6 H x0)^2 vanishes on the fold and
     nowhere else in the period; near the fold the proper distance grows with the square of the coordinate distance,
        (FD-6)  |sigma| = 3 H (x0 - pi/(12 H))^2 [1 + 6 H^2 (x0 - pi/(12 H))^2 + ...],
     so the two coordinate values on either side of x0 = pi/(12 H) at the same coordinate distance lie at the same proper
     distance from the fold: the coordinate line of x0 is folded onto the line of proper distances (a fold map, example 5).

What lives on the fold. In UM-3 the Standard Model (the Higgs doublet with the ad hoc vacuum, the gauge fields of
SU(3)_C x SU(2)_L x U(1)_Y, three generations of quarks and leptons and three right-handed neutrinos), the fold fluid and
the induced Einstein-Hilbert term of the fold live on the fold: they are fields at sigma = 0, functions of x1, ..., x4 (no
field depends on the extra times). Integrated over the extra times, the fold is the four-dimensional universe that we
observe, with the metric diag(e^(2 a4), e^(2 a4), e^(2 a4), -1) in x1, ..., x4. dirac16complex and gravity live in the
bulk sigma != 0 as well as on the fold; the bound states chi of dirac16complex are the part of it that the fold holds,
and the portals couple dirac16complex to the Standard Model at sigma = 0. In UM-3 files the word fold means this surface
and nothing else: a number of equal energy levels is written as a number of degenerate states, and a growth by powers of
Euler's number as a logarithm.

Examples of folds that are meaningful for UM-3.
  1. Our fold. The fold z = pi/2 of the period that contains our world (FD-1): the seven-dimensional world-volume of the
     Standard Model, and after the integration over the extra times the four-dimensional universe that we observe.
  2. The copies of the fold. Because the metric repeats with the period pi/(6 H), every surface
     x0 = pi/(12 H) + (an integer multiple of pi/(6 H)) is a copy of the fold, one per period. Neighbouring copies are
     separated by a tip (z a multiple of pi), where the warp (sin(z)^2)^(1/6) vanishes and g_x0x0 = cot(z)^2 diverges, and
     which lies at an infinite proper distance from both: in proper distance every copy has its own complete line
     -infinity < sigma < infinity. This is why the period pi/(6 H) of x0 produces no Kaluza-Klein tower with the spacing
     12 H; the x0 mass of the bound states is their binding to the fold.
  3. A folded sheet of paper. The crease of a folded sheet is a fold in this sense: the two halves are mirror images
     (property 1) joined along the crease, the sheet is continuous there and its direction changes abruptly (property 3).
     In UM-3 the direction across the crease is the hidden direction sigma, the seven directions along the crease are
     x1, ..., x7, and the crease is the fold.
  4. A folded function. The warp factor e^(-2 H |sigma|) is the simplest folded function: continuous, mirror symmetric,
     largest at sigma = 0, with a jump of its derivative,
        (FD-7)  d/d sigma e^(-2 H |sigma|) = -2 H sgn(sigma) e^(-2 H |sigma|),
                d^2/d sigma^2 e^(-2 H |sigma|) = 4 H^2 e^(-2 H |sigma|) - 4 H delta_D(sigma),
     whose delta function is the origin of the thin source of property 3. Every function of UM-3 that depends on sigma
     through |sigma| is folded at sigma = 0: the metric functions of FD-4 and the profiles of the bound states of
     dirac16complex (example 7).
  5. A fold map. In the mathematics of smooth maps the fold (Whitney's fold singularity) is the map u -> u^2 of a line onto
     a half-line: it folds the line at u = 0, two points +u and -u land on the same point, and the derivative of the map
     vanishes on the fold. Near the fold the map from the author's coordinate x0 to the distance |sigma| from the fold is
     of this kind (FD-6), and g_x0x0 = cot(z)^2, the square of the derivative d sigma/d x0, vanishes there.
  6. The brane of Randall and Sundrum. The five-dimensional metric
        (FD-8)  dy_RS^2 + e^(-2 k_RS |y_RS|) (dx1^2 + dx2^2 + dx3^2 - dx4^2),
                lambda_RS = 6 k_RS/kappa_5,   Lambda_RS = -6 k_RS^2/kappa_5
     (y_RS the proper coordinate across the brane, k_RS the inverse curvature length of the bulk, kappa_5 = 8 pi G_5) has a
     fold at y_RS = 0 with the properties 1 to 3 (its coordinate y_RS is already the proper distance, so property 4 does
     not arise); Einstein's equations require there a brane of the tension lambda_RS (Israel's junction condition) and in
     the bulk the vacuum energy Lambda_RS. The fold of UM-3 is of the same kind; it differs in that the time x4 is not
     warped, three extra times are warped together with ordinary space, and the Lovelock terms add to the junction
     conditions.
  7. A particle bound to a thin layer. A particle held by an attractive thin layer has a folded wave function: it falls
     off exponentially with the distance on both sides, and the layer makes its derivative jump (for the first-order
     Dirac equation, the wave function itself). In UM-3 the particles chi of dark matter are the states of dirac16complex
     bound to the fold; at rest and without their self-interaction (the field is
     Psi = e^(3 H |sigma|) chi(sigma) e^(-i omega_b x4))
        (FD-9)  chi(sigma) = e^(-q_b |sigma|) chi(0+) (sigma > 0),   chi(sigma) = e^(-q_b |sigma|) chi(0-) (sigma < 0),
                chi(0+) = exp( gamma^(0) (mu_L P_L + mu_R P_R) ) chi(0-),   omega_b = sqrt(m_Psi^2 - q_b^2),
     where mu_L, mu_R are the strengths of the fold for the left- and right-handed halves of dirac16complex (set by the
     Standard-Model fields on the fold), gamma^(0) = T^0 the Dirac matrix along sigma, P_L, P_R the chiral projectors,
     m_Psi the bulk mass, and q_b = -m_Psi (mu_L + mu_R) tanh(s)/(2 s), s = sqrt(mu_L mu_R) (q_b = -m_Psi mu_L/2 for
     mu_R = 0).
  8. The fold as a mirror for dirac16complex. The reflection across the fold acts on the profiles chi(sigma) in two ways,
        (FD-10)  (R_1 chi)(sigma) = T_0 T_1 T_2 T_3 chi(-sigma),   (R_2 chi)(sigma) = T_0 T_5 T_6 T_7 chi(-sigma)
     (T_a the author's Dirac matrices; for states at rest R_1 is the reflection across the fold combined with the
     reflection of ordinary space, R_2 the reflection across the fold combined with the reflection of the extra times).
     The Krein charge of a state is its share of the conserved charge of dirac16complex, which is indefinite: a state can
     carry the charge -1 or +1. R_1 is a symmetry of dirac16complex, of gravity and of the mean field of a gas of the
     particles chi: the four bound states of Krein charge -1 (the particles chi) are even under it and the four of Krein
     charge +1 are odd, so the mean field of the gas cannot mix the two signs of the indefinite charge. R_2 maps the bound
     states of one Krein charge onto those of the other and makes the two sets degenerate without the self-interaction.
  9. The planes of Horava and Witten. In M-theory on an interval (a circle whose points are identified with their mirror
     images), the two ten-dimensional planes left in place by the reflection are mirror surfaces (property 1); the gauge
     fields E8 x E8 live on them while gravity fills the bulk. This is the arrangement of UM-3, where the Standard Model
     lives on the fold and gravity and dirac16complex fill the bulk.

What is not a fold.
  * The tips z = 0 and z = pi (mod pi): the mirror exchanges them within a period, but there the warp vanishes, g_x0x0
    diverges, and they lie at an infinite proper distance; they carry no thin source.
  * A smooth maximum of a warp, such as 1/cosh(H sigma)^2: mirror symmetric and largest at sigma = 0, but without a kink
    and without a thin source.

euler.meaning: Euler's number, the base of the natural logarithm; $\mathrm{e}^{X}$ is the exponential of $X$.

diff.meaning: The differential: $\mathrm{d}X$ is an infinitesimal change of $X$, $\mathrm{d}X/\mathrm{d}Y$ the derivative of $X$ with respect to $Y$, $\mathrm{d}^nX$ the volume element of $n$ variables.

pi.meaning: The number pi, the ratio of the circumference of a circle to its diameter.

infty.meaning: Infinity: as a limit of an integral or a sum it means that the range has no bound.

diag.meaning: A diagonal matrix with the listed entries on its diagonal (in the order of the coordinates $x_0, x_1, \dots, x_7$ for a tensor of eight dimensions, $x_1, \dots, x_7$ for a tensor of the fold, $x_1, \dots, x_4$ for a four-dimensional tensor).

identity.meaning: The identity matrix of the size fixed by the context ($16 \times 16$ on dirac16complex, $4 \times 4$ on a four-dimensional spinor, $3 \times 3$ in generation or flavour space).

partial.meaning: A partial derivative: $\partial_M$ with respect to the coordinate $X^M$, $\partial_\mu$ with respect to $x^\mu$, $\partial_\sigma$ with respect to $\sigma$, $\partial X/\partial Y$ the derivative of $X$ with respect to $Y$ at fixed other variables.

nabla.meaning: The covariant derivative of a tensor with the Levi-Civita connection of the metric $g_{MN}$ (Christoffel symbols $\Gamma^P{}_{MN}$).

nablahat.meaning: The covariant derivative of the fold: with the Levi-Civita connection of the metric of the fold (for four-dimensional tensors of its metric $\hat h_{\mu\nu} = \mathrm{diag}(\mathrm{e}^{2a_4}, \mathrm{e}^{2a_4}, \mathrm{e}^{2a_4}, -1)$ in the observable coordinates $x_1, \dots, x_4$; for $\hat\nabla_a\mathcal{S}^a{}_b$ of the induced metric of the seven-dimensional fold).

delta.meaning: The Kronecker delta: with two indices $\delta^M_N = 1$ if $M = N$ and 0 otherwise (likewise $\delta_{X\mathrm{L}}$ is 1 if the label $X$ of a half of dirac16complex is L and 0 otherwise); with upper and lower index strings the generalised Kronecker delta $\delta^{M_1\cdots M_n}_{N_1\cdots N_n}$, the determinant of the $n \times n$ matrix of the Kronecker deltas $\delta^{M_a}_{N_b}$ ($+1$ or $-1$ if the upper indices are an even or odd permutation of the lower ones, 0 otherwise).

dagger.meaning: Hermitian conjugation: the complex conjugate of the transpose of a matrix or spinor (for field operators the adjoint operator).

star.meaning: Complex conjugation of a number, or of each entry of a matrix or column.

prime.meaning: The derivative of a function of the time $x_4$ alone with respect to $x_4$ ($a_4' = \mathrm{d}a_4/\mathrm{d}x_4$; two primes the second derivative); on a function of $\sigma$ alone (a profile) the derivative with respect to $\sigma$.

hc.meaning: The Hermitian conjugate of the preceding terms.

trace.meaning: The trace of a matrix: the sum of its diagonal entries.

iM.meaning: A coordinate index of eight dimensions (also with a numbered copy $M_1, M_2, \dots$): it runs over $x_0, x_1, \dots, x_7$; a repeated index is summed.

iN.meaning: A coordinate index of eight dimensions (also $N_1, N_2, \dots$), running over $x_0, \dots, x_7$; a repeated index is summed.

iP.meaning: A coordinate index of eight dimensions (also $P_1, P_2, \dots$), running over $x_0, \dots, x_7$; a repeated index is summed.

iQ.meaning: A coordinate index of eight dimensions (also $Q_1, Q_2, \dots$), running over $x_0, \dots, x_7$; a repeated index is summed.

iS.meaning: A coordinate index of eight dimensions, running over $x_0, \dots, x_7$; a repeated index is summed.

ia.meaning: A frame (orthonormal) index running over $0, 1, \dots, 7$ (frame direction $(0)$ along $\sigma$, $(1), (2), (3)$ along ordinary space, $(4)$ along the time, $(5), (6), (7)$ along the extra times); raised and lowered with the frame metric $\eta_{ab} = \mathrm{diag}(1, 1, 1, 1, -1, -1, -1, -1)$; on the fold ($a, b \in \{1, \dots, 7\}$) the frame of the fold; a repeated index is summed.

imu.meaning: A four-dimensional coordinate index running over the observable coordinates $x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4$ of the fold (signature $+,+,+,-$); a repeated index is summed.

iA.meaning: A colour (adjoint SU(3)) index running over $1, \dots, 8$; a repeated index is summed.

iI.meaning: A weak-isospin (adjoint SU(2)) index running over $1, 2, 3$; a repeated index is summed.

ii.meaning:
A generation index ($i = 1, 2, 3$), which also labels the neutrino mass states $
u_1, 
u_2, 
u_3$; in a frame component such as $\mathcal{S}^{(i)}{}_{(i)}$ a direction $x_i$ of ordinary space (the three components are equal); a repeated index is not summed unless a sum sign is written.

ij.meaning: A second generation or mass-state index (as $i$).

iX.meaning: The label of a half of dirac16complex: $X \in \{\mathrm{L}, \mathrm{R}\}$ (left-handed or right-handed half); a sum over $X$ runs over both.

if.meaning: The label of a kind of Standard-Model multiplet: $f \in \{Q, u, d, \ell, e, \nu\}$ (quark doublets, up-quark singlets, down-quark singlets, lepton doublets, charged-lepton singlets, right-handed neutrinos); a sum over $f$ runs over the six.

ipsi.meaning: The label of a Standard-Model fermion field in a sum: $\psi$ runs over $Q, u_{\mathrm{R}}, d_{\mathrm{R}}, \ell, e_{\mathrm{R}}, \nu_{\mathrm{R}}$.

ir.meaning: An extra-time direction of the fold: $r \in \{5, 6, 7\}$ ($x_5, x_6, x_7$); not summed (the three components are equal).

io.meaning: The label of a single-particle state of dirac16complex: a Kohn-Sham orbital, or a mode of the quantised field; a sum over $o$ runs over the orbitals or the modes.

Xcoord.meaning: The author's coordinates of the eight-dimensional spacetime, $X = \{x_0, x_1, \dots, x_7\}$ with the hidden direction first (Dirac_Einstein-Lovelock_4+4_Nash.nb, section DEFCHART); $X^M$ is the coordinate with the index $M$ and $\mathrm{d}^8X = \mathrm{d}x_0\,\mathrm{d}x_1\cdots\mathrm{d}x_7$ the coordinate volume element.

xfour.meaning: The coordinates of the fold: $x_i$ ($i = 1, 2, 3$) of ordinary space, $x_4$ the time, $x_r$ ($r = 5, 6, 7$) the extra times; a field of the fold is a function of the four observable coordinates $x = (x_1, x_2, x_3, x_4)$, and $\mathrm{d}^4x = \mathrm{d}x_1\,\mathrm{d}x_2\,\mathrm{d}x_3\,\mathrm{d}x_4$.

x0.meaning: The hidden space-like coordinate (listed first); the metric depends on it through $z = 6Hx_0$, periodically with the period $\pi/(6H)$.

x4.meaning: The time ($x_4 \ge 0$ in the ad hoc vacuum); a prime on a function of $x_4$ alone is $\mathrm{d}/\mathrm{d}x_4$.

x5.meaning: The first of the three extra time-like coordinates.

x6.meaning: The second of the three extra time-like coordinates.

x7.meaning: The third of the three extra time-like coordinates.

sigma.meaning: The proper coordinate of the hidden direction: $\mathrm{d}\sigma = \lvert\cot z\rvert\,\mathrm{d}x_0$, $\sigma = \mathrm{sgn}(\pi/2 - z)\ln(\sin z)/(6H)$ on one period $0 < z < \pi$; $\sigma = 0$ is the fold $z = \pi/2$, $\sigma \to \mp\infty$ the tips $z \to 0, \pi$; one period of $x_0$ is the whole line $-\infty < \sigma < \infty$.

zvar.meaning: The angle variable of the hidden direction, $z = 6Hx_0$; one period of $x_0$ is $0 < z < \pi$, the fold is $z = \pi/2$.

metric.meaning: The metric tensor of the eight-dimensional spacetime (signature $+,+,+,+,-,-,-,-$ in the order $x_0, \dots, x_7$): $g_{MN}\,\mathrm{d}X^M\mathrm{d}X^N$ is the squared interval, $g^{MN}$ its inverse, $\lvert g\rvert$ the absolute value of its determinant ($\sqrt{\lvert g\rvert}\,\mathrm{d}^8X$ is the proper volume element).

eta.meaning: The flat metric of the frame, $\eta = \mathrm{diag}(1, 1, 1, 1, -1, -1, -1, -1)$ (eta4488 of 4+4.nb); $\eta^{ab}$ is its inverse (the same matrix).

vielbein.meaning: The vielbein (frame field) of the metric: $g_{MN} = \eta_{ab}\,\mathbf{e}^a{}_M\mathbf{e}^b{}_N$; $\mathbf{e}_a{}^M$ is its inverse; $\mathbf{e}_{bN} = \eta_{bc}\mathbf{e}^c{}_N$; $\mathbf{e}^{(a)}$ is the frame one-form $\mathbf{e}^a{}_M\,\mathrm{d}X^M$.

Christoffel.meaning: The Christoffel symbols of the metric $g_{MN}$ (the Levi-Civita connection).

Riemann.meaning: The curvature of the metric $g_{MN}$: with four indices the Riemann tensor (convention $[\nabla_P, \nabla_Q]V^M = R^M{}_{NPQ}V^N$), with two indices the Ricci tensor $R_{MN} = R^P{}_{MPN}$, without indices the scalar curvature $R = g^{MN}R_{MN}$; with frame indices $R^{(a)(b)}{}_{(c)(d)}$ its frame components, $R^{(a)(b)}{}_{(a)(b)}$ (no sum) the sectional curvature of the frame plane $(a, b)$.

Hconst.meaning: The author's constant (an inverse length) that fixes the period $\pi/(6H)$ of $x_0$, the Lovelock couplings and the cosmological constant $\Lambda = -10H^2$; in UM-3 a free parameter.

a4.meaning: The author's metric function of the time $x_4$ that scales ordinary 3-space: on the fold $\mathrm{e}^{a_4}$ is the scale factor of cosmology and $a_4'$ the Hubble rate.

b4.meaning: The author's metric function of the time $x_4$ in the extra-time components, $b_4 > 0$, never identically 1 (the author's order of 2026-10-24); the scale factor of the extra times is $\mathrm{e}^{-a_4}b_4$ times the warp.

Stot.meaning: The action of UM-3 (the integral of the Lagrangian density over spacetime); its variation with respect to every field gives the field equations.

SEL.meaning: The Einstein-Lovelock action of gravity in eight dimensions.

Sstab.meaning: The action of the stabiliser of the bulk (a medium specified by its energy-momentum tensor $\mathcal{T}_{\mathrm{stab}}$).

SPsi.meaning: The action of dirac16complex in the bulk (kinetic term with the canonical spin connection, mass term, contact self-interaction).

Sfold.meaning: The action of the fold: the Standard Model, the portals of dirac16complex, the fold fluid and the induced gravity of the fold, all at $\sigma = 0$.

alphaL.meaning: The Lovelock coupling of order $p$, $\alpha_{(p)} = w_{(p)}H^{2-2p}$ ($\alpha_{(1)} = 1$).

LovL.meaning: The Lovelock density of order $p$ (a scalar built from $p$ Riemann tensors): $\mathcal{L}_{(1)} = R$ (Einstein-Hilbert), $\mathcal{L}_{(2)}$ the Gauss-Bonnet density, $\mathcal{L}_{(3)}$ the cubic Lovelock density.

Lambda.meaning: The eight-dimensional cosmological constant, $\Lambda = -10H^2$ (the author writes the pure number $\Lambda_{\mathrm{N}} = 10$ in $0 = -\Lambda_{\mathrm{N}} + \sum_p H^{-2p}w_{(p)}\mathcal{E}_{(p)}$).

LambdaN.meaning: The author's pure number in the vacuum equations of his notebook, $\Lambda_{\mathrm{N}} = 10$; $\Lambda = -\Lambda_{\mathrm{N}}H^2$.

Psi.meaning: dirac16complex: the author's 16-component complex spinor field of eight dimensions; $\bar\Psi = \Psi^\dagger\sigma_{16}$ is its Dirac adjoint; in a term of the fold, $\Psi$ is its value at $\sigma = 0$.

PsiL.meaning: The left-handed half of dirac16complex, $\Psi_{\mathrm{L}} = P_{\mathrm{L}}\Psi$ (the upper eight components in the basis of 4+4.nb).

PsiR.meaning: The right-handed half of dirac16complex, $\Psi_{\mathrm{R}} = P_{\mathrm{R}}\Psi$ (the lower eight components).

Tmat.meaning: The author's eight real $16 \times 16$ Dirac matrices T16^A[a] of 4+4.nb ($a = 0, \dots, 7$; $T_0, \dots, T_7$), with $\{T_a, T_b\} = 2\eta_{ab}\mathbf{1}$; $T^a = \eta^{ab}T_b$.

gammaM.meaning: The Dirac matrices of dirac16complex along the coordinates, $\gamma^M = \mathbf{e}_a{}^MT^a$, $\gamma_M = g_{MN}\gamma^N$; $\gamma^{(a)} = T^a$ along the frame direction $(a)$ ($\gamma^{(0)}$ along $\sigma$, $\gamma^{(4)}$ along the time).

sigma16.meaning: The matrix of the Dirac adjoint, $\sigma_{16} = T_0T_1T_2T_3$, real and symmetric; $\sigma_{16}T_a$ is real and antisymmetric.

Gamma8.meaning: The chirality matrix of eight dimensions, $\Gamma_8 = T_0T_1\cdots T_7$ (the author's T16^A[8]) $= \mathrm{diag}(-\mathbf{1}_8, \mathbf{1}_8)$; $\Gamma_8^2 = \mathbf{1}$; it anticommutes with every $T_a$.

PX.meaning: The chiral projector of the half $X$: $P_X = P_{\mathrm{L}}$ for $X = \mathrm{L}$, $P_{\mathrm{R}}$ for $X = \mathrm{R}$.

Dcov.meaning: The covariant derivative: on dirac16complex $D_M = \partial_M + \Omega_M$ (with $D_M\bar\Psi = \partial_M\bar\Psi - \bar\Psi\Omega_M$); on the fields of the fold the gauge and spin covariant derivative $D_\mu$ (the partial derivative plus the spin connection of the fold and the gauge fields times their couplings and generators); $D^\mu = \hat h^{\mu\nu}D_\nu$; on an adjoint field $(D_\mu X)^A = \partial_\mu X^A + g_3f^{ABC}G^B_\mu X^C$ (likewise for $SU(2)$ with $g_2\epsilon^{IJK}$).

mPsi.meaning: The mass parameter of dirac16complex in the bulk.

lamPsi.meaning: The coupling of the contact self-interaction of dirac16complex.

Omega.meaning: The spin connection acting on dirac16complex, $\Omega_M = \frac12\varpi_{Mab}\Sigma^{ab}$.

omegaSC.meaning: The canonical (Levi-Civita) spin connection of the vielbein, antisymmetric in $a, b$.

SigmaGen.meaning: The generators of Spin(4,4) on dirac16complex, $\Sigma^{ab} = \frac14[T^a, T^b]$ (the scaled commutators of the author's matrices); $\Sigma^{\mu\nu} = \mathbf{e}_a{}^\mu\mathbf{e}_b{}^\nu\Sigma^{ab}$ along the fold.

Tstab.meaning: The energy-momentum tensor of the stabiliser of the bulk (frame components): the source that a static bulk of the author's metric requires, found and named by Claude (Anthropic) on 2026-10-24.

rhos.meaning: The energy density of the stabiliser; with frozen extra times it is the energy density of the bulk at which ordinary space stands still.

ps.meaning: The pressure of the stabiliser (equal along $\sigma$, ordinary space and the extra times).

Vstar.meaning: The physical volume of the extra times $x_5, x_6, x_7$ on the fold in the late universe, $V_* = V_{\mathrm{t}}(\mathrm{e}^{-a_4}b_4)^3$ (with $V_{\mathrm{t}} = \int\mathrm{d}x_5\,\mathrm{d}x_6\,\mathrm{d}x_7$ the coordinate volume of the extra times) at a time when $\mathrm{e}^{-a_4}b_4$ is constant; it converts the eight-dimensional normalisation into the four-dimensional one.

Vt.meaning: The coordinate volume of the (compact) extra times, $V_{\mathrm{t}} = \int\mathrm{d}x_5\,\mathrm{d}x_6\,\mathrm{d}x_7$.

Zfold.meaning: The fold factor, $\mathcal{Z}(x_4) = V_{\mathrm{t}}(\mathrm{e}^{-a_4}b_4)^3/V_*$: the factor by which the size of the extra times multiplies every term of the fold; $\mathcal{Z} = 1$ when the extra times are frozen at their late value.

Ffold.meaning: Any function of the fields at the fold (used to state a rule of integration).

hhat.meaning:
The four-dimensional metric of the fold, $\hat h_{\mu
u} = \mathrm{diag}(\mathrm{e}^{2a_4}, \mathrm{e}^{2a_4}, \mathrm{e}^{2a_4}, -1)$ in the coordinates $x_1, \dots, x_4$ (the induced metric at $\sigma = 0$ without the extra times); $\hat h^{\mu
u}$ its inverse, $\hat h$ its determinant, $\sqrt{-\hat h} = \mathrm{e}^{3a_4}$; $\hat h^{(1)}_{\mu
u}$ its first-order cosmological perturbation.

Rhat.meaning: The scalar curvature of the metric $\hat h_{\mu\nu}$ of the fold.

kappa4.meaning: The coupling of the induced gravity of the fold, $\kappa_4 = 8\pi G_{\mathrm{ind}}$; four-dimensional gravity on the fold has $8\pi G_{\mathrm{N}} = \kappa_4/(1 + 5\epsilon_{\mathrm{r}}/6)$ (the Friedmann equation of the fold to first order in $\epsilon_{\mathrm{r}}$).

LIG.meaning: The Lagrangian of the induced gravity of the fold.

Lff.meaning: The Lagrangian of the fold fluid (only its energy-momentum tensor $\mathcal{T}_{\mathrm{ff}}$ enters the equations).

Tff.meaning: The energy-momentum tensor of the fold fluid (frame components of the fold, four-dimensional normalisation).

rhoff.meaning: The energy density of the fold fluid.

pff.meaning: The pressure of the fold fluid along ordinary space.

qff.meaning: The pressure of the fold fluid along the extra times.

LH.meaning: The Lagrangian of the Higgs doublet on the fold.

Lgauge.meaning: The Lagrangian of the gauge fields of $SU(3)_C\times SU(2)_L\times U(1)_Y$ on the fold.

Lf.meaning: The kinetic Lagrangian of the quarks and leptons on the fold.

LY.meaning: The Yukawa Lagrangian of the quarks and leptons with the Higgs doublet.

LP.meaning: The Lagrangian of the portals of dirac16complex at the fold.

Phi.meaning: The Higgs doublet (two complex components, hypercharge $1/2$), a field of the fold.

muH.meaning: The mass parameter of the Higgs potential, $\mu^2 < 0$ (it enters only as $\mu^2$).

lamH.meaning: The quartic coupling of the Higgs potential, $\lambda > 0$.

vev.meaning: The vacuum expectation value of the lower component of the Higgs doublet, $v^2 = -\mu^2/\lambda$.
vev.value: 246.22 GeV $= (\sqrt2\,G_{\mathrm{F}})^{-1/2}$ with the Fermi constant $G_{\mathrm{F}} = 1.1663788\times10^{-5}$ GeV$^{-2}$ of the muon lifetime (Particle Data Group)

hHiggs.meaning: The Higgs field: the fluctuation of the lower component of the Higgs doublet about $v$.

Aadhoc.meaning: The author's ad hoc upper component of the Higgs vacuum, almightyAdHoc, $\mathcal{A}(x_4) = v_{\mathcal{A}}\mathrm{e}^{-2a_{40}x_4}$.

vA.meaning: The amplitude of almightyAdHoc at $x_4 = 0$; the author's almightyAdHoc $= \mathrm{Exp}[-2\,a_{40}\,x_4]$ has $v_{\mathcal{A}} = 1$ in the units of his notebook.
vA.value: 1 in the units of the author's notebook; UM-3 keeps it free (the examples take $v_{\mathcal{A}} = v$ and $10v$)

a40.meaning: The decay constant of almightyAdHoc, $a_{40} > 0$: $\mathcal{A}$ falls by $\mathrm{e}$ in the time $1/(2a_{40})$.

omegahat.meaning: The spin connection of the four-dimensional metric $\hat h_{\mu\nu}$ of the fold acting on four-dimensional spinors.

g1.meaning: The $U(1)_Y$ gauge coupling (usually $g'$; not normalised for grand unification).

Ggluon.meaning: The gluon field of $SU(3)_C$ on the fold ($A = 1, \dots, 8$) and its field strength.

Wsu2.meaning: The gauge field of $SU(2)_L$ on the fold, $W^1_\mu, W^2_\mu, W^3_\mu$, and its field strength.

Bhyp.meaning: The hypercharge gauge field of $U(1)_Y$ on the fold and its field strength.

tgen.meaning: The generators of $SU(3)$ on colour triplets, $t^A = \lambda_{\mathrm{GM}}^A/2$ (the Gell-Mann matrices halved), $\mathrm{tr}(t^At^B) = \delta^{AB}/2$.

taupauli.meaning: The Pauli matrices acting on weak doublets ($\tau^1, \tau^2, \tau^3$; $\tau^2$ is the second one, not a square).

Yhyp.meaning: The hypercharge of a field, the charge of its coupling $g_1Y_fB_\mu$ to the hypercharge field in the covariant derivative ($1/6$, $2/3$, $-1/3$, $-1/2$, $-1$, $0$ for $Q, u_{\mathrm{R}}, d_{\mathrm{R}}, \ell, e_{\mathrm{R}}, \nu_{\mathrm{R}}$, $1/2$ for $\Phi$).

epsLC.meaning: The Levi-Civita symbol of three indices (the structure constants of $SU(2)$), $\epsilon^{123} = 1$.

psiSM.meaning: A Standard-Model fermion field (a four-dimensional Weyl field of the fold with three generations, written as a four-component spinor of fixed chirality); $\bar\psi = \psi^\dagger\beta$; $\psi_f$ the fields of the kind $f$.

gammahat.meaning:
The four-dimensional complex $4 	imes 4$ Dirac matrices of the fold, $\hat\gamma^\mu = \hat{\mathbf{e}}_a{}^\mu\hat\gamma^{(a)}$, $\{\hat\gamma^\mu, \hat\gamma^
u\} = -2\hat h^{\mu
u}\mathbf{1}$; $\hat\gamma_\mu = \hat h_{\mu
u}\hat\gamma^
u$.

betaD.meaning: The matrix of the four-dimensional Dirac adjoint, $\beta = \hat\gamma^{(4)}$ (Hermitian, $\beta^2 = \mathbf{1}$).

Qdoub.meaning: The left-handed quark doublets of the three generations, $Q = (u_{\mathrm{L}}, d_{\mathrm{L}})$ (colour triplets, hypercharge $1/6$).

uR.meaning: The right-handed up-type quarks $u, c, t$ (singlets of $SU(2)_L$, hypercharge $2/3$).

dR.meaning: The right-handed down-type quarks $d, s, b$ (hypercharge $-1/3$).

ell.meaning: The left-handed lepton doublets of the three generations, $\ell = (\nu_{\mathrm{L}}, e_{\mathrm{L}})$ (hypercharge $-1/2$).

eR.meaning: The right-handed electron, muon and tau (singlets, hypercharge $-1$).

Yuk.meaning: The Yukawa matrices ($3 \times 3$ complex matrices in generation space) of the up quarks, the down quarks, the charged leptons and the neutrinos.

cPhi.meaning: The Higgs-portal coupling of the left-handed half of dirac16complex (the right-handed half has none).

cG.meaning: The gluon-kinetic portal coupling of the half $X$ of dirac16complex.

cW.meaning: The $W$-kinetic portal coupling of the half $X$.

cB.meaning: The $B$-kinetic portal coupling of the half $X$.

ddip.meaning: The dipole-portal coupling of the half $X$ of dirac16complex with the hypercharge field strength.

Ddip.meaning: The dipole (antisymmetric tensor) density of the half $X$ of dirac16complex at the fold, $\mathcal{D}_X^{\mu\nu} = \mathrm{i}\bar\Psi\Sigma^{\mu\nu}P_X\Psi$ (real, DERIVED).

cf.meaning: The current-portal coupling of the half $X$ of dirac16complex with the fermion-number current of the multiplets of kind $f$ (flavour blind); $c^{\ell}_X$ and $c^{\nu}_X$ are those of the lepton doublets and of the right-handed neutrinos.

Jcur.meaning: The fermion-number current of the Standard-Model multiplets of kind $f$, $J_f^\mu = \bar\psi_f\hat\gamma^\mu\psi_f$ summed over the three generations and the gauge components; with other labels the currents that are the sources of the gauge fields.

jcur.meaning: The convective current of the half $X$ of dirac16complex, $j_X^\mu = \mathrm{i}(\bar\Psi P_XD^\mu\Psi - (D^\mu\bar\Psi)P_X\Psi)$ (real and joining the half with itself, DERIVED).

ip.meaning: The Lovelock order $p = 1, 2, 3$ (Einstein, Gauss-Bonnet, cubic), as an index and as a number; in the Kohn-Sham equations a second label of a Kohn-Sham orbital (as $o$, with $\delta_{op}$ the Kronecker delta of the two labels).

LovE.meaning: The Lovelock tensor of order $p$: the variation of $\sqrt{\lvert g\rvert}\,\mathcal{L}_{(p)}$ with respect to the metric ($\mathcal{E}_{(1)}$ the Einstein tensor, $\mathcal{E}_{(2)}$ the Gauss-Bonnet tensor); with frame indices its frame components.

isigma.meaning: The label $\sigma$ in $\partial_\sigma$: the derivative with respect to the proper hidden coordinate $\sigma$.

TPsi.meaning: The energy-momentum tensor of dirac16complex, $\mathcal{T}_{MN} = -(2/\sqrt{\lvert g\rvert})\,\delta S_\Psi/\delta g^{MN}$.

Tbulk.meaning: The energy-momentum tensor of all sources of the bulk, $\mathcal{T}_\Psi + \mathcal{T}_{\mathrm{stab}}$; $\mathcal{T}_{\mathrm{bulk}}{}^{(0)}{}_b$ is its flux along $\sigma$ (frame components).

Sfoldsrc.meaning: The thin source of the fold: its energy-momentum tensor per unit proper length across the fold (eight-dimensional normalisation, frame components along the fold); it is fixed by the jump of the first $\sigma$-derivatives of the metric across the fold (the junction conditions; $\kappa\mathcal{S}$ is the jump of the junction potential).

varepsilon.meaning: The half-thickness of a layer around the fold, taken to zero.

Fpot.meaning: The junction potential: a function of the first $\sigma$-derivatives of the metric functions whose derivatives are the coefficients of the second $\sigma$-derivatives in $\sum_p\alpha_{(p)}\mathcal{E}_{(p)}{}^a{}_b$ (FE-4).

fwarp.meaning: Any one of the three metric functions $\mathfrak{a}, \mathfrak{b}, \mathfrak{n}$ of the general warped metric (FE-34).

awarp.meaning: The logarithm of the scale factor of ordinary space in the general warped metric FE-34, a function of $\sigma$ and $x_4$; for the author’s metric $\mathfrak{a} = a_4 - H\lvert\sigma\rvert$; $\mathfrak{a}_n$ its term of order $n$ in the power series FE-35 ($\mathfrak{a}_1$ the first-order term).

bwarp.meaning: The logarithm of the scale factor of the extra times in the general warped metric FE-34; for the author’s metric $\mathfrak{b} = \ln b_4 - a_4 - H\lvert\sigma\rvert$; $\mathfrak{b}_n$ its term of order $n$ ($\mathfrak{b}_1$ the first-order term).

nwarp.meaning: The logarithm of the lapse in the general warped metric FE-34 ($g_{x_4x_4} = -\mathrm{e}^{2\mathfrak{n}}$); for the author’s metric $\mathfrak{n} = 0$; $\mathfrak{n}_n$ its term of order $n$ ($\mathfrak{n}_1$ the first-order term).

TH.meaning: The energy-momentum tensor of the Higgs doublet (four-dimensional normalisation).

Tgauge.meaning: The energy-momentum tensor of the gauge fields.

Tf.meaning: The energy-momentum tensor of the quarks and leptons.

TP.meaning: The energy-momentum tensor of the portals of dirac16complex.

TIG.meaning: The energy-momentum tensor of the induced gravity of the fold, $\mathcal{T}_{\mathrm{IG}}{}^\mu{}_\nu = -\hat G^\mu{}_\nu/\kappa_4$.

Tany.meaning: The energy-momentum tensor of any one term of the fold (in $\mathcal{T}^r{}_r = \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{fold}}$).

Lfold.meaning: The Lagrangian of any one term of the fold (four-dimensional normalisation).

LPsi.meaning: The Lagrangian of dirac16complex, the square bracket of IN-4.

Ghat.meaning: The Einstein tensor of the four-dimensional metric $\hat h_{\mu\nu}$ of the fold.

Mfold.meaning: The fold operator of dirac16complex: the $16 \times 16$ matrix (with a derivative along the fold) built from the Standard-Model fields at the fold by varying the portals with respect to $\bar\Psi$ (FE-13).

Theta.meaning: The Yukawa source of the Higgs equation, $\Theta = -\partial\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Y}}/\partial\Phi^\dagger$ (a doublet of fermion bilinears).

uL.meaning: The upper (up-type, left-handed) components of the quark doublets.

dL.meaning: The lower (down-type, left-handed) components of the quark doublets.

nuL.meaning: The upper (neutral, left-handed) components of the lepton doublets: the left-handed neutrinos.

eL.meaning: The lower (charged, left-handed) components of the lepton doublets.

Kport.meaning: The portal factors of the gauge kinetic terms, $\mathcal{K}_{G} = 1 + \sum_Xc^{G}_X\bar\Psi P_X\Psi$ (likewise for $W$ and $B$): the gauge couplings at the fold are divided by $\sqrt{\mathcal{K}}$.

Jcolour.meaning: The colour current of the quarks.

Jweak.meaning: The weak-isospin current of the left-handed fermion doublets.

JPhi.meaning: The weak-isospin current of the Higgs doublet (it contains the mass terms of the $W$ fields); $J_\Phi^{2\,x_4}$ its isospin charge density with $I = 2$.

JY.meaning: The hypercharge current of the fermions and of the Higgs doublet.

Vport.meaning: The vector potential that dirac16complex exerts on the Standard-Model fermions of kind $f$ through the current portals, $\mathcal{V}^{f}_\mu = \sum_Xc^{f}_Xj_{X\mu}$ ($\mathcal{V}^{Q}, \mathcal{V}^{u}, \dots, \mathcal{V}^{\nu}$ for the six kinds); flavour blind.

Rres.meaning: The residuals of the ad hoc Higgs vacuum in the upper ($\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{A}}$) and lower ($\mathcal{R}_v$) components of the Higgs equation: what the ad hoc vacuum leaves unbalanced.

Asf.meaning: The expansion rate of ordinary space in units of $H$, $\mathsf{A} = a_4'/H$.
Asf.value: 1 at the author's vacuum, 0 at the static block; $H_4^{(0)}/H$ today ($H_4^{(0)}$ the Hubble constant)

Usf.meaning: The rate of change of $b_4$ in units of $H$, $\mathsf{U} = b_4'/(Hb_4)$.

A1sf.meaning: The time derivative of $\mathsf{A}$ in units of $H$, $\mathsf{A}_1 = \mathsf{A}'/H = a_4''/H^2$.

U1sf.meaning: The time derivative of $\mathsf{U}$ in units of $H$, $\mathsf{U}_1 = \mathsf{U}'/H$.

Gfac.meaning: The factor of the $(\sigma, x_4)$ bulk equation of the author’s metric, $\mathcal{G} = 5\mathsf{A}^2(\mathsf{A} - \mathsf{U})^2 - 6\mathsf{A}^2 + 6\mathsf{A}\mathsf{U} + \mathsf{U}^2 + 1$.

rhobulk.meaning: The energy density of the bulk sources, $\rho_{\mathrm{bulk}} = -\mathcal{T}_{\mathrm{bulk}}{}^{(4)}{}_{(4)}$.

is.meaning: A second extra-time direction of the fold (as $r$, different from it).

inn.meaning: The order $n = 1, 2, \dots$ of a term of the power series of the metric (also its exponent of $\epsilon_{\mathrm{r}}$); $\mathfrak{a}_n$, $\mathfrak{b}_n$, $\mathfrak{n}_n$ are the terms of order $n$.

epsr.meaning: The bookkeeping parameter of the response of the bulk to the matter of the fold: the ratio of the bulk to the fold gravity, $\epsilon_{\mathrm{r}} = \kappa_4V_*/(\kappa H)$.
epsr.value: below $1.344\times10^{-13}$: the four-dimensional gravitational wave has $c_{\mathrm{g}}^2 = (96 + 83\epsilon_{\mathrm{r}})/(96 + 82\epsilon_{\mathrm{r}})$, and the gravitational waves and the light of the neutron-star merger GW170817 arrived together, $(c_{\mathrm{g}} - 1) < 7\times10^{-16}$

epsc.meaning: The bookkeeping parameter of the cosmological perturbations of the metric of the fold (the size of the CMB anisotropies).

omegafreq.meaning: A frequency: the energy of a mode $\propto \mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{i}\omega x_4}$ ($\omega_o$ of the orbital $o$).

chiprof.meaning: The profile of a mode of dirac16complex along the hidden direction, $\Psi = \mathrm{e}^{3H\lvert\sigma\rvert}\chi(\sigma)\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm{i}(\vec k\cdot\vec x - \omega x_4)}$ (a 16-component spinor function of $\sigma$); as a four-dimensional field, $\chi$ denotes the particle of a bound state.

chib.meaning: The profile of a state of dirac16complex bound to the fold.

kvec.meaning: The (comoving) momentum along ordinary space, $\vec k^2$ its square.

xvec.meaning: The position in ordinary space, $\vec x = (x_1, x_2, x_3)$.

gammavec.meaning: The three frame Dirac matrices of dirac16complex along ordinary space, $\vec\gamma = (\gamma^{(1)}, \gamma^{(2)}, \gamma^{(3)})$.

Kbulk.meaning: The transfer matrix of the profile equation at zero momentum, $\chi' = \mathbb{K}\chi$.

qdecay.meaning: The decay rate of a profile along $\sigma$ at frequency $\omega$, $q = \sqrt{m_\Psi^2 - \omega^2}$ (imaginary in the continuum).

psigma.meaning: The momentum along the hidden direction (local wave number of a profile along $\sigma$).

kappavec.meaning: A momentum along the extra times (three components); the fields of UM-3 have $\vec\kappa = 0$.

muX.meaning: The dimensionless strengths of the fold for the left-handed and right-handed halves of dirac16complex, set by the mean fields of the Standard Model at the fold: the jump of the profile across the fold is the exponential of $\gamma^{(0)}(\mu_{\mathrm{L}}P_{\mathrm{L}} + \mu_{\mathrm{R}}P_{\mathrm{R}})$; negative values attract.

mean.meaning: The mean (expectation) value of an operator in the state of the medium (the vacuum, a plasma, the Kohn-Sham state).

Gsq.meaning: The mean square of the gluon field strength, $\langle G^A_{\mu\nu}G^{A\mu\nu}\rangle$ (the gluon condensate in the QCD vacuum, a thermal value in the plasma).

Wsq.meaning: The mean square of the $SU(2)$ field strength, $\langle W^I_{\mu\nu}W^{I\mu\nu}\rangle$.

Bsq.meaning: The mean square of the hypercharge field strength, $\langle B_{\mu\nu}B^{\mu\nu}\rangle$.

nf.meaning: The number density of the Standard-Model fermions of kind $f$ (particles minus antiparticles, summed over generations and gauge components), the time component of the mean current $\langle J_f^\mu\rangle$ in the rest frame of the medium.

qb.meaning: The inverse width of a state of dirac16complex bound to the fold: its profile falls as $\mathrm{e}^{-q_{\mathrm{b}}\lvert\sigma\rvert}$.

varsigma.meaning: The auxiliary variable of the bound-state condition, $\varsigma = \sqrt{\mu_{\mathrm{L}}\mu_{\mathrm{R}}}$ ($\varsigma_- = \sqrt{-\mu_{\mathrm{L}}\mu_{\mathrm{R}}}$ when $\mu_{\mathrm{L}}\mu_{\mathrm{R}} < 0$).

omegab.meaning: The energy of a state of dirac16complex bound to the fold at zero momentum: the four-dimensional mass of the particle $\chi$.

ns.meaning: The scalar density of dirac16complex in the Kohn-Sham state, $n_{\mathrm{s}} = \langle\bar\Psi\Psi\rangle = \mathrm{tr}\,\mathcal{N}$.

Nmat.meaning: The one-body density matrix of dirac16complex, $\mathcal{N} = \sum_o\mathsf{n}_o\varphi_o\bar\varphi_o$ (a $16 \times 16$ matrix at each point).

KSorb.meaning: A Kohn-Sham orbital of dirac16complex (a single-particle solution of FE-41) and its Dirac adjoint.

nocc.meaning: The occupation of the Kohn-Sham orbital $o$ (between 0 and 1).

Eorb.meaning: An energy: $E_o$ the energy of the Kohn-Sham orbital $o$; in the neutrino sector the energy of a neutrino.

QPsi.meaning: The conserved charge of dirac16complex (the Noether charge of a change of the phase of $\Psi$ by a constant), a Krein form (indefinite).

Bkrein.meaning: The Krein operator, $\mathfrak{B} = \mathrm{i}\sigma_{16}\gamma^{(4)}$: a Hermitian involution with the signature (8, 8); $\Psi^\dagger\mathfrak{B}\Psi$ is the charge density.

Qorb.meaning: The charge $Q_\Psi$ (the Krein charge) of the single-particle state $o$ of dirac16complex, a Kohn-Sham orbital or a mode: $+1$ or $-1$ for a normalised state.

chiKS.meaning: The profile of the occupied Kohn-Sham orbital $o$ ($o = 1, \dots, 4$, the four positive-energy states of the bound level) of a homogeneous gas of the particles $\chi$ at rest on the static block: a 16-component spinor function of $\sigma$; the orbital of each particle is $\mathrm{e}^{3H\lvert\sigma\rvert}\chi_o(\sigma)\mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{i}\omega x_4}$ divided by the square root of the volume of ordinary space and of $V_*$; normalised to the Krein charge $-1$, $\int\mathrm{d}\sigma\,\chi_o^\dagger\mathfrak{B}\chi_o = -1$; $\bar\chi_o = \chi_o^\dagger\sigma_{16}$ is its Dirac adjoint.

GKS.meaning: The dimensionless strength of the self-interaction of the gas of particles $\chi$ in the Kohn-Sham states: the self-coupling $\lambda_\Psi$ times the number density $n_\chi$ of the particles on the fold divided by the volume $V_*$ of the extra times, $G_{\mathrm{KS}} = \lambda_\Psi n_\chi/V_*$ (in units of $m_\Psi$ when numbers are given).

Mmean.meaning: The mean field of the self-interaction in the Kohn-Sham equation of the gas: the $16 \times 16$ matrix $\lambda_\Psi(n_{\mathrm{s}}\mathbf{1} - \mathcal{N})$ at each $\sigma$, which adds to the mass $m_\Psi$; positive (repulsive) for $\lambda_\Psi > 0$.

Minf.meaning: The limit of the mean field far from the fold where the proper density of the gas has saturated: the matrix for which the local equation has a solution decaying exactly at the rate $3H$.

rhohat.meaning: The scalar density of the occupied orbitals, $\hat\rho = \frac14\sum_o\bar\chi_o\chi_o$ (per particle); the scalar density of the gas is $n_{\mathrm{s}} = (n_\chi/V_*)\,\mathrm{e}^{6H\lvert\sigma\rvert}\hat\rho$.

rhohatinf.meaning: The constant that the proper scalar density $\mathrm{e}^{6H\lvert\sigma\rvert}\hat\rho$ approaches far from the fold where it saturates.

rhohatL.meaning: The scalar density of the left-handed half of the occupied orbitals, $\hat\rho_{\mathrm{L}} = \frac14\sum_o\bar\chi_oP_{\mathrm{L}}\chi_o$; at the fold the mean of its values on the two sides.

rhohatL0.meaning: The left-handed scalar density $\hat\rho_{\mathrm{L}}$ of the bound state without the self-interaction and without the Higgs feedback.

Nhat.meaning: The one-body density matrix of the occupied orbitals, $\hat{\mathcal{N}} = \frac14\sum_o\chi_o\bar\chi_o$ (a $16 \times 16$ matrix at each $\sigma$, per particle); the density matrix of the gas is $\mathcal{N} = (n_\chi/V_*)\,\mathrm{e}^{6H\lvert\sigma\rvert}\hat{\mathcal{N}}$.

Eint.meaning: The interaction energy per particle of the gas of $\chi$: the mean self-interaction energy $\frac{\lambda_\Psi}{2}(n_{\mathrm{s}}^2 - \mathrm{tr}\,\mathcal{N}^2)$ integrated across the hidden direction, per particle.

epsp.meaning: The energy per particle of the gas of $\chi$: the orbital energy minus the interaction energy per particle, which the orbital energy counts twice.

wchi.meaning: The equation of state of the gas of the particles $\chi$: its pressure divided by its energy density, $w_\chi = P_{\mathrm{KS}}/(n_\chi\epsilon_{\mathrm{p}})$ (0 for cold dark matter, $-1$ for a vacuum energy).

PKS.meaning: The pressure of the gas of $\chi$ along ordinary space in the Kohn-Sham state: the particles are at rest, so it is the mean self-interaction, $P_{\mathrm{KS}} = n_\chi\mathsf{E}_{\mathrm{int}}$.

muL0.meaning: The strength $\mu_{\mathrm{L}}$ of the fold for the left-handed half without the feedback of the gas on the Higgs field.

kappaH.meaning: The strength of the Higgs-portal loop of the gas: the gas without the feedback changes the local $v_{\mathrm{loc}}^2$ at the fold by the factor $1 - \kappa_{\mathrm{H}}$, $\kappa_{\mathrm{H}} = c_\Phi n_\chi\hat\rho_{\mathrm{L}0}(0)/(\lambda v^2V_*)$; negative where the Higgs portal binds the fold ($c_\Phi < 0$, $\hat\rho_{\mathrm{L}0}(0) > 0$): the gas raises $v_{\mathrm{loc}}^2$.
kappaH.value: $-0.3$ in the test of the loop

Delta.meaning: A change, difference or small variation of the quantity that follows (for example an interval of the time, a perturbation of a density, a difference of two squared masses, or an addition to an effective number of species).

geff.meaning: The effective (canonically normalised) gauge couplings of the fold when the fold factor is $\mathcal{Z}$, $g_{k,\mathrm{eff}} = g_k/\sqrt{\mathcal{Z}}$ ($k = 1, 2, 3$).

Yeff.meaning: The effective Yukawa matrices, $\mathcal{Y}/\sqrt{\mathcal{Z}}$ (for each of $\mathcal{Y}^{u}, \mathcal{Y}^{d}, \mathcal{Y}^{e}, \mathcal{Y}^{\nu}$).

GNeff.meaning: The effective Newton constant of the fold, $G_{\mathrm{N}}/\mathcal{Z}$.

GN.meaning: Newton’s constant of four-dimensional gravity (the gravity of our world, on the fold), $G_{\mathrm{N}} = 1/M_{\mathrm{Pl}}^2$ with the Planck mass $M_{\mathrm{Pl}} = 1.221\times10^{19}$ GeV.

GF.meaning: The Fermi constant, $G_{\mathrm{F}} = 1/(\sqrt2\,v^2)$ in the Standard-Model vacuum (its measured value); in FE-45 the Fermi constant of the ad hoc vacuum, which is $G_{\mathrm{F,loc}}$ of FE-49.

mh.meaning: The mass of the Higgs boson.

Aphoton.meaning: The photon field: the massless combination of $W^1, W^2, W^3$ and $B$ (canonically normalised).

nI.meaning: The unit isovector of the ad hoc vacuum, $n = (2\mathcal{A}v, 0, \mathcal{A}^2 - v^2)/(\mathcal{A}^2 + v^2)$, which fixes which combination of $W^1, W^2, W^3$ joins $B$ in the photon.

Umix.meaning: The unitary $3 \times 3$ matrices that diagonalise the mass matrices of the up quarks, the down quarks, the charged leptons and the neutrinos (left-handed and right-handed rotations).

mferm.meaning: The masses of the quarks ($m_u, m_c, m_t$; $m_d, m_s, m_b$), of the charged leptons ($m_e, m_\mu, m_\tau$) and of the three neutrino mass states ($m_1, m_2, m_3$, Dirac masses).
mferm.value: measured values; $\Delta m_{21}^2 = 7.41\times10^{-5}$ eV$^2$, $\lvert\Delta m_{31}^2\rvert = 2.511\times10^{-3}$ eV$^2$ in the computations of UM-3 (the global fit NuFIT 5.2 of the oscillation data, November 2022), $7.49\times10^{-5}$ and $2.513\times10^{-3}$ eV$^2$ in NuFIT 6.0 (2024); the lightest mass $m_1 = 0$ in the computations, below 4.12 meV by DESI DR2 with the CMB

Pmns.meaning: The lepton mixing matrix (Pontecorvo-Maki-Nakagawa-Sakata) of the three Dirac neutrinos; $U_{\alpha i}$ are its entries.
Pmns.value: $\theta_{12} = 33.40^\circ$, $\theta_{23} = 49.14^\circ$, $\theta_{13} = 8.54^\circ$ (NuFIT 5.2, November 2022, normal ordering, with the Super-Kamiokande atmospheric data); the Dirac phase is set to zero (ASSUMED; the fit prefers $197^\circ$)

nugen.meaning: A neutrino field: $\nu_\alpha$ the flavour states ($\alpha = e, \mu, \tau$), $\nu_i$ the mass states ($i = 1, 2, 3$).

LCC.meaning: The charged-current interaction of the quarks and leptons with the $W$ bosons.

hatferm.meaning: The left-handed quarks and charged leptons in the mass basis ($\hat e_{\mathrm{L}\alpha}$ the charged lepton of flavour $\alpha$).

gport.meaning: The four-dimensional couplings of the bound states $\chi$ of dirac16complex to the Standard Model (FE-47): to $\Phi^\dagger\Phi$, to the gluon kinetic density, to the number densities of the fermions of kind $f$, and the Yukawa coupling of the Higgs boson to $\chi$.

vhat.meaning: The direction of motion of a neutrino: the unit vector $\hat v = \vec p/\lvert\vec p\rvert$ ($\hat v_{\vec p}$, $\hat v_{\vec q}$ for the momenta $\vec p$, $\vec q$), and the four-vector $\hat v^\mu = (1, \hat v)$ in the order $(x_4; x_1, x_2, x_3)$; $\mathrm{d}^2\hat v$ is the element of solid angle of the directions.

nablavec.meaning: The gradient along ordinary space, $\vec\nabla = (\partial_{x_1}, \partial_{x_2}, \partial_{x_3})$ (in the local frame of the medium).

pvec.meaning: The momentum of a neutrino (three components along ordinary space, in the rest frame of the medium); $\lvert\vec p\rvert = E$ for a neutrino of negligible mass.

qvec.meaning: The momentum of another neutrino of the medium (the integration variable of the neutrino-neutrino potential); $\mathrm{d}^3\vec q$ its volume element.

rhoflav.meaning: The $3 \times 3$ flavour density matrices of the neutrinos and of the antineutrinos of momentum $\vec p$ in the basis $e, \mu, \tau$: the diagonal entries are the occupation numbers of the three flavours, the off-diagonal entries the coherence between the flavours; $\bar\varrho$ is defined with the flavour indices in the reversed order, so that it obeys an equation of the same form.

Hflav.meaning: The flavour Hamiltonians ($3 \times 3$ Hermitian matrices) of the neutrinos and of the antineutrinos of momentum $\vec p$.

Ccoll.meaning: The collision terms ($3 \times 3$ matrices) of the neutrinos and the antineutrinos of momentum $\vec p$: the rates of change of $\varrho_{\vec p}$ and $\bar\varrho_{\vec p}$ by emission, absorption, scattering and pair processes with the matter.

Mmass.meaning: The diagonal matrix of the squared masses of the three neutrino mass states, $\mathsf{M}^2 = \mathrm{diag}(m_1^2, m_2^2, m_3^2)$ ($\mathsf{M}$ appears only squared).

Vm.meaning: The matter potential of the neutrinos (a $3 \times 3$ matrix in flavour space) from their forward scattering on the electrons, positrons and neutrons of the medium.

Vnunu.meaning: The neutrino-neutrino potential (a $3 \times 3$ matrix in flavour space) from the forward scattering of a neutrino on the other neutrinos and antineutrinos of the medium; it depends on their flavour content and their directions.

VPsi.meaning: The potential energy that dirac16complex gives every neutrino through the current portal of the lepton doublets, $V_\Psi = \mathcal{V}^{\ell}_{x_4}$ (the same for the three flavours).

vloc.meaning: The local value of the electroweak vacuum, $v_{\mathrm{loc}}^2 = 2\langle\Phi^\dagger\Phi\rangle$: it sets the local masses of the quarks and leptons (each mass times $v_{\mathrm{loc}}/v$) and the local Fermi constant; $v_{\mathrm{loc}} = v$ in the Standard-Model vacuum.
vloc.value: $v$ in the late universe outside dense dirac16complex

GFloc.meaning: The local Fermi constant, $G_{\mathrm{F,loc}} = 1/(\sqrt2\,v_{\mathrm{loc}}^2)$ ($= G_{\mathrm{F}}$ where $v_{\mathrm{loc}} = v$).

ne.meaning: The number density of electrons (bound and free; in a supernova all are free, in the recombining universe $x_{\mathrm{e}}n_e$ is the density of the free electrons).

thetamix.meaning: The vacuum mixing angle of two neutrino flavours (in the two-flavour description of a resonance, one of the three angles $\theta_{12}, \theta_{13}, \theta_{23}$ of $U_{\mathrm{PMNS}}$).

thetam.meaning: The mixing angle of two neutrino flavours in matter.

mmass.meaning: A mass: $m_i$ the mass of the neutrino mass state $i$; in $\Delta m^2$ the squared-mass difference of two neutrino mass states ($m_2^2 - m_1^2$ for the two states of a resonance, multiplied by $v_{\mathrm{loc}}^2/v^2$ where this differs from 1).

VCC.meaning: The charged-current matter potential of the electron neutrinos (forward scattering on electrons through $W$ exchange).

neres.meaning: The electron density at which the flavour conversion in matter is resonant (the Mikheyev-Smirnov-Wolfenstein resonance).

PLZ.meaning: The probability that a neutrino jumps between the eigenstates of matter at the resonance (Landau-Zener); $P_{\mathrm{LZ}} = 0$ is an adiabatic resonance.

rrad.meaning: The distance from the centre of the star along the path of a neutrino.

res.meaning: The label of a quantity evaluated at the resonance, where $n_e = n_{e,\mathrm{res}}$.

GELN.meaning: The angular distribution of the electron lepton number carried by the neutrinos minus that carried by the heavy-lepton neutrinos, per unit solid angle of the direction $\hat v$, multiplied by $\sqrt2G_{\mathrm{F,loc}}$.

Focc.meaning: The occupation numbers of the electron neutrinos, of the electron antineutrinos, and of one heavy-lepton neutrino and antineutrino ($x = \mu$ or $\tau$), as functions of the energy $E$ and the direction $\hat v$ (the diagonal entries of $\varrho_{\vec p}$ and $\bar\varrho_{\vec p}$); in a transport code, the same for the number of particles in an energy bin.

etaM.meaning: The Minkowski metric of the four-vectors $\hat v^\mu$, $\eta_{\mathrm{M}} = \mathrm{diag}(1, -1, -1, -1)$ in the order $(x_4; x_1, x_2, x_3)$.

Omegafw.meaning: The (complex) frequency of a flavour wave of the neutrino gas, measured from the shift caused by the potentials; an imaginary part greater than zero is an instability.

Kvec.meaning: The (real) wave vector of a flavour wave of the neutrino gas, measured from the shift caused by the potentials.

deltaFC.meaning: The occupation (or number per energy bin) of electron neutrino-antineutrino pairs converted into heavy-lepton pairs by the flavour equipartition FE-52; a negative value converts heavy-lepton pairs into electron pairs.

rhob.meaning: The (rest-mass) energy density of the baryons: in a supernova the local density of the matter (quoted in g/cm$^3$), in cosmology the mean density of the baryons ($\rho_{\mathrm{b}}^{(0)}$ today).

rhoFC.meaning: The baryon density below which the flavour equipartition FE-52 is applied (the critical density $\rho_{\mathrm{c}}$ of Gogilashvili and Tamborra).

x4b.meaning: The time of the bounce of the collapsing stellar core.

tFC.meaning: The time after the bounce from which the flavour equipartition FE-52 is applied.

Neff.meaning: The effective number of neutrino species: the energy density of the relativistic particles other than photons in units of that of one neutrino species whose temperature is $(4/11)^{1/3}$ times that of the photons.

rhonu.meaning: The energy density of the neutrinos and antineutrinos of all flavours.

rhogamma.meaning: The energy density of the photons.

Tnu.meaning: The temperature of the cosmic neutrino background; $\mathsf{T}_\nu^{(0)}$ its value today.

Tgamma.meaning: The temperature of the photons (of the CMB); $\mathsf{T}_\gamma^{(0)}$ its value today.

nnu.meaning: The number density of the cosmic neutrino background per flavour (neutrinos plus antineutrinos, one helicity each); $n_\nu^{(0)}$ its value today.

ascale.meaning: The scale factor of the fold, $a = \mathrm{e}^{a_4}$ (normalised to 1 today by the choice of the comoving coordinates $x_1, x_2, x_3$), and its first and second derivatives with respect to the conformal time $\tau_{\mathrm{c}}$.

tauc.meaning: The conformal time of the fold, $\mathrm{d}\tau_{\mathrm{c}} = \mathrm{d}x_4/a$; a dot on a quantity of the cosmological perturbations is $\mathrm{d}/\mathrm{d}\tau_{\mathrm{c}}$.

Hconf.meaning: The conformal expansion rate, $\mathcal{H} = \dot a/a = a\,a_4'$.

psiB.meaning: The Bardeen potential of the time-time part of the perturbed metric of the fold (the Newtonian potential) in the conformal Newtonian gauge, a function of $\tau_{\mathrm{c}}$ and of the wave number $k$, and its derivative with respect to $\tau_{\mathrm{c}}$.

phiB.meaning: The Bardeen potential of the space-space part of the perturbed metric of the fold (the curvature potential) in the conformal Newtonian gauge, and its first and second derivatives with respect to $\tau_{\mathrm{c}}$.

kwave.meaning: The comoving wave number of a Fourier mode of the perturbations, $k = \lvert\vec k\rvert$.

rhotot.meaning: The total energy density of the matter of the fold (all species); $\Delta\rho$ its perturbation.

Ptot.meaning: The total pressure of the matter of the fold; $\Delta\mathcal{P}$ its perturbation.

varthetatot.meaning: The divergence of the velocity of the total matter: $(\rho + \mathcal{P})\vartheta$ is the sum over the species of their energy density plus pressure times the divergence of their velocity.

Sigmas.meaning: The anisotropic stress (shear) of the total matter: $(\rho + \mathcal{P})\Sigma_{\mathrm{s}}$ is the sum over the species (photons and neutrinos) of their energy density plus pressure times their shear.

deltachi.meaning: The density contrast of the dark matter (the bound states $\chi$ of dirac16complex), the perturbation of its energy density divided by its mean, and its derivative with respect to $\tau_{\mathrm{c}}$.

varthetachi.meaning: The divergence of the velocity of the dark matter (for a Fourier mode, $\mathrm{i}k$ times its velocity along the wave vector), and its derivative.

deltab.meaning: The density contrast of the baryons and its derivative.

varthetab.meaning: The divergence of the velocity of the baryons and its derivative.

deltagamma.meaning: The density contrast of the photons and its derivative.

varthetagamma.meaning: The divergence of the velocity of the photons and its derivative.

deltanu.meaning: The density contrast of the relativistic neutrinos and its derivative.

varthetanu.meaning: The divergence of the velocity of the relativistic neutrinos and its derivative.

Sigmagamma.meaning: The anisotropic stress (shear) of the photons.

Sigmanu.meaning: The anisotropic stress (shear) of the relativistic neutrinos.

Gammachib.meaning: The rate (per conformal time) at which the dark matter exchanges momentum with the baryons through the portal couplings of FE-47 (elastic scattering of $\chi$ on nuclei and electrons).
Gammachib.value: negligible for the couplings that direct detection allows

cs.meaning: The sound speed of the baryon gas: its square is the temperature of the gas divided by the mean mass per particle, times one minus a third of the logarithmic derivative of that temperature with respect to $a$.

xe.meaning: The ionisation fraction: the fraction of the electrons that are free.

sigmaT.meaning: The Thomson cross-section of the scattering of photons on free electrons.

Rbg.meaning: The ratio of the inertia of the baryons to that of the photons, $\mathsf{R} = 3\rho_{\mathrm{b}}/(4\rho_\gamma)$.

rhochi.meaning: The energy density of the dark matter, the bound states $\chi$ of dirac16complex; $\rho_\chi^{(0)}$ its value today.

il.meaning: The multipole index and number ($l = 0, 1, 2, \dots$) of an expansion in Legendre polynomials of the direction of a photon or a neutrino relative to the wave vector, or of the CMB sky in spherical harmonics.

Fgamma.meaning: The multipoles of the temperature perturbation of the photons ($\mathsf{F}_0 = \delta_\gamma$, $\mathsf{F}_1 = 4\vartheta_\gamma/(3k)$, $\mathsf{F}_2 = 2\Sigma_\gamma$; the $F_{\gamma l}$ of Ma and Bertschinger) and their derivatives with respect to $\tau_{\mathrm{c}}$.

Ggamma.meaning: The multipoles of the polarisation perturbation of the photons (the $G_{\gamma l}$ of Ma and Bertschinger) and their derivatives.

Nnu.meaning:
The multipoles of the perturbation of the relativistic neutrinos ($\mathsf{N}_0 = \delta_
u$, $\mathsf{N}_1 = 4\vartheta_
u/(3k)$, $\mathsf{N}_2 = 2\Sigma_
u$) and their derivatives.

Upsilonnu.meaning: The multipoles of the relative perturbation of the distribution of a massive neutrino state at the comoving momentum $\mathsf{q}$ (the $\Psi_l$ of Ma and Bertschinger) and their derivatives.

qcom.meaning: The comoving momentum of a neutrino, $a\lvert\vec p\rvert$.

Ecom.meaning: The comoving energy of a massive neutrino ($a$ times its energy).

Fzero.meaning: The unperturbed (Fermi-Dirac) occupation number of the cosmic neutrino background at the comoving momentum $\mathsf{q}$.

rs.meaning: The comoving sound horizon at the drag epoch: the comoving distance that a sound wave of the photon-baryon fluid travels until the baryons are released from the photons.

taud.meaning: The conformal time of the drag epoch, when the baryons are released from the photons (redshift about 1060).

csgb.meaning: The sound speed of the tightly coupled photon-baryon fluid.

DM.meaning: The transverse comoving distance (comoving angular-diameter distance) to the redshift $\mathsf{z}$, for a spatially flat fold.

DH.meaning: The Hubble distance at the redshift $\mathsf{z}$.

DV.meaning: The volume-averaged distance to the redshift $\mathsf{z}$.

H4.meaning: The expansion rate (Hubble rate) of the fold, $H_4 = a_4'$, as a function of the time or of the redshift; $H_4^{(0)}$ its value today, the Hubble constant.

Cl.meaning: The angular power spectra of the CMB at the multipole $l$: temperature with temperature, temperature with E-mode polarisation, E-mode polarisation with itself.

CMBlab.meaning: The labels of the CMB observables: $\mathrm{T}$ the temperature anisotropy, $\mathrm{E}$ the E-mode (gradient) polarisation; $\mathrm{TT}$, $\mathrm{TE}$, $\mathrm{EE}$ label the spectra of their products.

Itrans.meaning: The transfer functions of the CMB: the multipole $l$ of the temperature or E-mode anisotropy today produced by a Fourier mode $k$ of unit primordial curvature perturbation, computed from FE-54 and FE-55 (the line-of-sight integral).

PRspec.meaning: The primordial power spectrum of the comoving curvature perturbation, per logarithmic interval of $k$.

As.meaning: The amplitude of the primordial curvature spectrum at the pivot $k_*$.

nS.meaning: The spectral index of the primordial curvature spectrum.

kstar.meaning: The pivot wave number of the primordial spectrum.

Omegachi.meaning: The density parameter of the dark matter today.

Omegab.meaning: The density parameter of the baryons today.

OmegaL.meaning: The density parameter of the dark energy (the vacuum energy of the fold) today.

Omeganu.meaning: The density parameter of the neutrinos of the CNB: $\Omega_\nu$ that of the massive states today; $\Omega_\nu^{(i)}(\mathsf{z})$ the energy density of the mass state $i$ at the redshift $\mathsf{z}$ in units of the critical density today.

h100.meaning: The present expansion rate of the fold in units of 100 km/s/Mpc.

rhoc.meaning: The critical density, the energy density of a spatially flat fold at the expansion rate $H_4$; $\rho_{\mathrm{c}}^{(0)}$ its value today.

rhoL.meaning: The vacuum energy density of the fold, the dark energy of UM-3: $\rho_\Lambda = \rho_{\mathrm{ff}} - 31HV_*/(4\kappa)$ (FE-59).

TSM.meaning: The energy-momentum tensor of the Standard Model on the fold, $\mathcal{T}_{\mathrm{H}} + \mathcal{T}_{\mathrm{gauge}} + \mathcal{T}_{\mathrm{f}}$.

Jgeo.meaning: The jump of the junction potential across the fold computed from the metric: the geometric side of the junction condition $\mathcal{J} = \kappa\mathcal{S}$, which equates it to $\kappa$ times the energy-momentum tensor $\mathcal{S}$ of everything on the fold.

rhoSM.meaning: The energy density of the Standard-Model particles.

grho.meaning: The effective number of relativistic degrees of freedom of the energy density.
grho.value: 106.75 in the Standard Model above the electroweak scale

gs.meaning: The effective number of relativistic degrees of freedom of the entropy density.

Ttemp.meaning: The temperature of the Standard-Model plasma (of the photons after the annihilation of electrons and positrons).

sent.meaning: The entropy density of the Standard-Model plasma.

nchi.meaning: The number density of the dark-matter particles $\chi$ (particles plus antiparticles).

nchieq.meaning: The number density of $\chi$ in thermal equilibrium with the plasma (non-relativistic).

gchi.meaning: The number of internal states of the bound level of $\chi$ that are in thermal equilibrium.

sigmaann.meaning: The annihilation cross-section of the particles $\chi$ into Standard-Model particles (through the portals) in the normalisation of FE-61, where $n_\chi$ counts the four particle and the four antiparticle states of the bound level: $\langle\sigma_{\mathrm{ann}}\mathsf{v}\rangle$ is a quarter of the annihilation rate $(\sigma\mathsf{v})_{\chi\bar\chi}$ of one particle $\chi_a$ with one antiparticle $\bar\chi_a$.

vrel.meaning: The relative velocity of two annihilating particles; $\langle\sigma_{\mathrm{ann}}\mathsf{v}\rangle$ is the thermal average of the product.

xf.meaning: The ratio of the mass of $\chi$ to the temperature at which its annihilations stop (freeze-out).

gstar.meaning: The effective number of relativistic degrees of freedom at the freeze-out ($g_\rho$ there).

rhonuR.meaning: The energy density of the three right-handed neutrinos.

CnuR.meaning: The collision term of the right-handed neutrinos: the rate at which collisions produce (or remove) their energy density.

Tdec.meaning: The temperature at which the right-handed neutrinos decouple from the plasma.

qSM.meaning: The pressure of the Standard Model along the extra times at the fold: the mean on-shell Lagrangian density of the Standard-Model fields (the extra-time component of the energy-momentum tensor of every term of the fold is its Lagrangian, because the fields of the fold do not depend on the extra times).

qchi.meaning: The pressure of the bound states of dirac16complex along the extra times, integrated across the fold (their on-shell Lagrangian, the self-interaction energy per volume; zero for a dilute gas).

qP.meaning: The pressure of the portals along the extra times: their mean on-shell Lagrangian density.

Cdiff.meaning: The amplitude of the difference mode S-6, the only static first-order correction of the metric when the bulk medium does not respond: $\mathfrak{a}_1' = -\mathfrak{b}_1' = C_{\mathrm{d}}\mathrm{e}^{6H\lvert\sigma\rvert}$.

crad.meaning: The amplitude of the radion mode: the first-order jumps at the fold $([\mathfrak{a}_1'], [\mathfrak{b}_1'], [\mathfrak{n}_1']) = c_{\mathrm{rad}}(1, -1, 5)$, which change only the extra-time component of the junction.

Deltar.meaning: The mismatch of the radion condition: the sum over the matter of the fold of its pressure along the extra times and $(\rho - 3\mathcal{P})/2$ (zero for radiation).

Orot.meaning: The $2 \times 2$ isospin rotation by the angle $\phi_{\mathrm{rot}}$ about the second isospin axis (a real element of $SU(2)$).

phirot.meaning: The angle of the isospin rotation that turns $(0, V_{\mathrm{rad}})/\sqrt2$ into the ad hoc vacuum: $\tan(\phi_{\mathrm{rot}}/2) = \mathcal{A}/v$.

Vrad.meaning: The modulus of the Higgs doublet in the ad hoc vacuum, $V_{\mathrm{rad}} = \sqrt{v^2 + \mathcal{A}^2}$ ($V_{\mathrm{rad}}^2 = 2\Phi^\dagger\Phi$).

Rrad.meaning: The radial residual of the Higgs equation FE-15 in the ad hoc vacuum written as a gauge rotation (S-10): the amount by which $V_{\mathrm{rad}}$ fails to solve the radial equation; zero for a solution.

us.meaning: The rescaled profile of a massless scalar field of the bulk at zero momentum along ordinary space: the field is $\mathrm{e}^{3H\lvert\sigma\rvert}u_{\mathrm{s}}(\sigma)\,\mathrm{e}^{-\mathrm{i}\omega x_4}$.

csc.meaning: The limiting speed of the zero mode of a scalar field of the bulk along ordinary space, in units of the speed of light on the fold.

cgauge.meaning: The limiting speed of the zero mode of a gauge field (a photon) of the bulk, in units of the speed of light on the fold.

cfer.meaning: The limiting speed of the zero mode of a fermion of the bulk with the kink mass $M_{\mathrm{k}}\,\mathrm{sgn}(\sigma)$, in units of the speed of light on the fold.

cgrav.meaning: The limiting speed of the zero mode of the transverse traceless graviton (the four-dimensional gravitational wave) at the static block or with frozen extra times, in units of the speed of light on the fold.
cgrav.value: $\sqrt{15/2} = 2.74$ for the bulk alone; $\sqrt{83/82} = 1.0061$ with the graviton term of the fold from the Gauss-Bonnet and cubic Lovelock terms; $\sqrt{(96 + 83\epsilon_{\mathrm{r}})/(96 + 82\epsilon_{\mathrm{r}})}$ with the induced gravity of the fold

Mkink.meaning: The mass of a fermion of the bulk that changes sign at the fold (a kink mass $M_{\mathrm{k}}\,\mathrm{sgn}(\sigma)$), used to illustrate the speeds of bulk fermions.

cb.meaning: The limiting speed of the bound particles $\chi$ of dirac16complex along ordinary space, in units of the speed of light on the fold (first order in the momentum).

H2flav.meaning: The two-flavour Hamiltonian of the electron neutrinos in the Sun (the mass states 1 and 2 with the potential $\cos^2\theta_{13}V_{\mathrm{CC}}$; the third state decouples).

thetaij.meaning: The three mixing angles of $U_{\mathrm{PMNS}}$ (its fourth parameter is the Dirac phase, which does not enter the electron-flavour results of UM-3).
thetaij.value: $33.40^\circ$, $8.54^\circ$, $49.14^\circ$ in the computations of UM-3 ($\sin^2\theta_{12} = 0.303$, $\sin^2\theta_{13} = 0.02203$, $\sin^2\theta_{23} = 0.572$: NuFIT 5.2, November 2022, normal ordering, with the Super-Kamiokande atmospheric data); $33.71^\circ$, $8.56^\circ$, $43.28^\circ$ in NuFIT 6.0 (2024; $\sin^2\theta_{12} = 0.308$, $\sin^2\theta_{13} = 0.02215$, $\sin^2\theta_{23} = 0.470$)

NA.meaning: Avogadro's number: $245N_{\mathrm{A}}$ cm$^{-3}$ is 245 moles of electrons per cubic centimetre.

Pee.meaning: The survival probability of electron neutrinos: the probability that an electron neutrino is detected as an electron neutrino.

P2.meaning: The survival probability of the two-flavour problem of the mass states 1 and 2 (S-20).

Pc.meaning: The crossing probability: the probability that a neutrino jumps from one eigenstate of matter to the other on its way through the Sun (exact for an exponential profile, Petcov).

rprod.meaning: The radius at which the solar neutrinos of a given reaction are produced.

rsunscale.meaning: The scale height of the electron density of the Sun, $r_\odot = R_\odot/10.54$.

Ye.meaning: The electron fraction of stellar matter: the number of electrons per nucleon.

mamu.meaning: The atomic mass unit, the mass per nucleon of stellar matter to within one per cent: $n_e = Y_e\rho/m_{\mathrm{u}}$.

gammaLZ.meaning: The adiabaticity parameter of a resonance: the jump probability of FE-50 is $\exp(-\pi\gamma_{\mathrm{LZ}}/2)$; $\gamma_{\mathrm{LZ}} \gg 1$ is adiabatic.

rres.meaning: The radius of a resonance: where the electron density equals $n_{e,\mathrm{res}}$ of FE-50 ($r_{\mathrm{H}}$ for $\Delta m^2_{31}$, $r_{\mathrm{L}}$ for $\Delta m^2_{21}$).

Kr.meaning: The wave number of a flavour wave along the radial direction (the radial component of $\vec K$).

ucos.meaning: The cosine of the angle between the direction of motion of a neutrino and the radial direction ($\mathsf{u}_e$, $\mathsf{u}_{\bar e}$ the edges of the emission cones of the electron neutrinos and antineutrinos).

Qflav.meaning: The amplitude of a small flavour coherence (the off-diagonal entry of $\varrho$) of the neutrinos moving with the direction cosine $\mathsf{u}$, in a flavour wave.

Qheat.meaning: The rate at which the absorption of electron neutrinos and antineutrinos heats the matter of the gain region (energy per time and mass).

Lspec.meaning: The luminosity (energy per time) of one neutrino species leaving the neutrinosphere.

Espec.meaning: The mean energy of one neutrino species.

alphas.meaning: The shape (pinching) parameter of a neutrino spectrum (Keil, Raffelt and Janka).

Yield.meaning: The yield of the particles $\chi$: their number density divided by the entropy density, $\mathsf{Y} = n_\chi/s$ (constant when they neither annihilate nor are produced).

Yieldeq.meaning: The yield of $\chi$ in thermal equilibrium, $n_{\chi,\mathrm{eq}}/s$.

xmass.meaning: The ratio of the mass of $\chi$ to the temperature, $\mathsf{x} = \omega_{\mathrm{b}}/\mathsf{T}$ (the time variable of the freeze-out).

Kbessel.meaning: The modified Bessel function of the second kind of order 2 ($K_2(y) \approx \sqrt{\pi/(2y)}\,\mathrm{e}^{-y}$ for large $y$).

sigmapair.meaning: The cross-section of the annihilation of one particle $\chi_a$ with one antiparticle $\bar\chi_a$ of the same species, summed over the final states; $\sigma_{\mathrm{pair}}\mathsf{v}$ its product with the relative velocity (a constant for s-wave annihilation).

sigmaSI.meaning: The spin-independent cross-section of the scattering of $\chi$ on a nucleon (normalised per nucleon, as the direct-detection limits are quoted).

mured.meaning: The reduced mass of $\chi$ and a nucleon, $\omega_{\mathrm{b}}m_{\mathrm{N}}/(\omega_{\mathrm{b}} + m_{\mathrm{N}})$.

fN.meaning: The effective coupling of $\chi$ to a nucleon in the coherent scattering (a vector or scalar contact interaction).

gportql.meaning: The current-portal couplings $\mathfrak{g}_f$ of FE-47 taken equal for all chiral quark states ($\mathfrak{g}_{\mathrm{q}}$) or for the nine chiral lepton states that take part, the six of the lepton doublets and the three right-handed charged leptons ($\mathfrak{g}_{\mathrm{l}}$), and the coupling to the proton that the lepton loop induces ($\mathfrak{g}_{\mathrm{p}}$).

qtransfer.meaning: The momentum transfer of the scattering of $\chi$ on a xenon nucleus in a detector.

fH.meaning: The nucleon matrix element of the Higgs coupling: the fraction of the nucleon mass carried by the quark masses and, through the trace anomaly, by the gluons.

nnuReq.meaning: The number density of the three right-handed neutrinos and their antiparticles in thermal equilibrium at the temperature $\mathsf{T}$.

Omegagamma.meaning: The density parameter of the photons today.

Tnueff.meaning: The effective temperature of the neutrinos that carries $N_{\mathrm{eff}}$ (the convention of CAMB).

Ifd.meaning: The Fermi-Dirac energy integral of a neutrino state with the mass-to-temperature ratio $y$; $\mathsf{I}(0) = 7\pi^4/120$.

yarg.meaning: The ratio of the mass of a neutrino state to its temperature, the argument of $\mathsf{I}$.

chisq.meaning: The chi-square of a comparison of a model with data (written $\chi^2$ in the text): the squared deviations weighted with the inverse covariance.

Xvec.meaning: The vectors of the model values and of the measured values of a data set (binned CMB spectra, BAO distances).

Cmat.meaning: The covariance matrix of the measured values; $\mathsf{C}^{-1}$ its inverse.

Xbin.meaning: A model value of the binned CMB spectrum, for the bin $b$ of the plik-lite binning.

wbin.meaning: The Planck weight of the multipole $l$ in its bin.

GammaCnuB.meaning: The rate at which a tritium target captures neutrinos of the cosmic neutrino background.

NT.meaning: The number of tritium nuclei of the target.

sigmabarT.meaning: The averaged cross-section of the capture of an electron neutrino on tritium: a tritium nucleus captures left-handed electron neutrinos of mean speed $\mathsf{s}$ and number density $n$ at the rate $\bar\sigma_{\mathrm{T}}(1 + \mathsf{s})\,c\,n$ ($c$ the speed of light, 1 in the formulas; Long, Lunardini and Sabancilar).

Uei.meaning: The electron row of the mixing matrix, $U_{\mathrm{e}i} = (U_{\mathrm{PMNS}})_{ei}$: $\lvert U_{\mathrm{e}i}\rvert^2$ is the electron-flavour fraction of the mass state $i$.

sstate.meaning: The mean speed of the neutrino mass state $i$ today, averaged over its momentum distribution (0 for a state at rest, 1 for a massless one).

ph.meaning: The momentum along the hidden direction of a particle confined to it, if that direction were compact (A-2, not UM-3).

mKK.meaning: The masses of the tower of modes of a field on a compact hidden direction (Kaluza-Klein masses; A-2, not UM-3).

kint.meaning: An integer that numbers the modes of a compact direction.

ellb.meaning: The width of a bound state of dirac16complex along the hidden direction: the root mean square of $\sigma$ in its density $\mathrm{e}^{-2q_{\mathrm{b}}\lvert\sigma\rvert}$.

Tchi.meaning: The four-dimensional energy-momentum tensor of the gas of the bound particles $\chi$ of dirac16complex, per proper volume of ordinary space at the fold (energy density $\rho_\chi$).

ellg.meaning: The length measured along the surface of a globe; $\mathrm{d}\ell_{\mathrm{g}}$ is the length of a small step on it (an example of a metric, not UM-3).

Rglobe.meaning: The radius of a globe (an example, not UM-3).

thglobe.meaning: The angle of a point of a globe from its north pole: 0 at the north pole, $\pi/2$ on the equator, $\pi$ at the south pole (an example, not UM-3).

phglobe.meaning: The longitude of a point of a globe (an example, not UM-3).
